text.p: - The number of unemployed rose 2.2 percent in December month-on-month and fell 1.8 percent year-on-year, the unemployment office said.
- Slovenian Finance Minister Mitja Gaspari reviewed financial and taxation policy over the past five years and presented future plans to finance ministers of EU members and associate EU members.
- Presentation of the Slovenia's government line-up to the parliamentary board starts on Tuesday with hearings of ministerial candidates.
- It is not likely that prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek will name his candidates for the legislative and agricultural ministries on Tuesday, sources close to parliament said.
- Investments in Slovenian industry in 1995 rose 48.7 percent to 333.2 billion tolars ($2.24 billion), the statistical office reported.
- The number of Slovenians visiting the Croatian coast in 1996 increased 46 percent versus 1995 to 437,604, the Tourist Association at the Slovenian Chamber of Economy said.

- The conservative Christian Democrats said they would not support the government line-up proposed by prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek and that they would propose their partners in the rightist "Spring" alliance do likewise.
